2. In `src/batchIngestor.mjs`:

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. I haven't edited the repo or written the plan file: the only write allowed was the plan file at `cfg\plans\…`, and I didn't create it. The plan is below.

## Diagnosis

**`src/queryDsl.mjs`**
- **String scanning (`tokenizeDsl`, lines 26–40):**
  - The closing quote is detected with `expr[j-1] !== '\\'`. That makes `"C:\\temp\\"` look like an escaped quote and never terminate.
  - Escapes are never decoded, so `\\` stays as two characters.
  - A dangling backslash is not detected.
- **Precedence (`parseExpr`, `parsePrimary`):**
  - AND and OR are folded left to right at one level, so `a OR b AND c` parses as `(a OR b) AND c`.
  - `NOT` calls `parsePrimary`. That works for `NOT x == 1`, but `NOT NOT x` and `NOT (…)` need a dedicated unary level.
- **Comparison semantics (`parsePrimary` closure):**
  - `==` and `!=` use strict equality, so `null` and `undefined` are not equal.
  - The relational operators use JS coercion, so `undefined > -1` is false but `null >= 0` is true. Both need to be false.
  - `NaN` must also be handled.
- **Missing paths:** `resolveField` already returns `undefined` for missing paths. Keep it.

**`src/batchIngestor.mjs`**
- `flush()` splices the buffer and awaits `sinkFn` with no lock. Concurrent flushes can run the sink in parallel and reorder batches.
- If the sink rejects, the batch is lost. The visible test expects `pendingCount` to stay 2.
- A rejection must put the batch back in front of any items ingested during the await.

## Implementation plan

### 1. `src/queryDsl.mjs`

**String scanning in `tokenizeDsl`**
- Replace the string branch with a loop that walks `j`.
- On `\\`:
  - If `j+1` is past the end of the input, throw `ERR_DSL_SYNTAX` ("dangling escape").
  - Otherwise map `\\`→`\`, `"`→`"`, `n`→newline, `t`→tab.
  - I recommend throwing `ERR_DSL_SYNTAX` for any other escape. The spec lists only four, so this is my call.
  - Advance by 2.
- On an unescaped `"`, end the string.
- If the input ends first, throw `ERR_DSL_SYNTAX` ("unterminated").

**Grammar**
- `parseOr` → `parseAnd` (joined by `OR`) → `parseNot` → `parsePrimary`.
- Each of the first two loops on its own operator.
- `parseNot` handles `NOT` recursively: `NOT` followed by `parseNot`, returning `!inner`.
- `parsePrimary` handles `(`, then `parseOr`, then `)`, or a comparison.
- Replace the `parseExpr()` call at the end with `parseOr()`.
- Keep the trailing-token check, so an unmatched `)` still throws.

**Comparison helper**
- `const isNil = v => v === null || v === undefined;`
- `const isBad = v => isNil(v) || (typeof v === 'number' && Number.isNaN(v));`
- `==`: if both sides are nil, `true`; otherwise `actual === target`.
- `!=`: the negation of `==`.
- `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`: if `isBad(actual) || isBad(target)`, return `false`; otherwise compare normally.

### 2. `src/batchIngestor.mjs`

- Add a private field `#tail = Promise.resolve()`.
- `flush()`:
  - Run `#flushLocked` as `const run = this.#tail.then(() => this.#flushLocked())`.
  - Set `this.#tail = run.catch(() => {})` so one failure doesn't poison the queue.
  - `return run`.
- `#flushLocked()` runs only inside the queue:
  - If the buffer is empty, return `{ flushedCount: 0 }`.
  - `const batch = this.#buffer.splice(0)`.
  - `try { await this.#sinkFn(batch); } catch (e) { this.#buffer.unshift(...batch); throw e; }`
  - On success, update the watermark with the max `seq` and add `batch.length` to `#totalCommitted`.
  - Return `{ flushedCount }`.
- `ingest()`:
  - Keep the validation and the push synchronously, so nothing is dropped.
  - Keep `await this.flush()` when `length >= maxBatchSize`.
  - The queue serializes it with other flushes.
  - A queued flush that finds an empty buffer is a no-op, so nothing is double-delivered.
- Ordering holds: the batch is restored at the front, and the lock means no later batch can reach the sink before the failed one is retried.

### 3. Constraints
- No `eval` or `new Function`.
- Leave `src/frozenWire.mjs` and `src/errors.mjs` untouched.

## Verification
- Run `node --test test/task_visible.test.mjs`.
- Add extra checks, ad hoc or in a new test file:
  - **Strings**
    - `"a\"b"`, `"\n"` and `"\t"` decode correctly.
    - `"abc\` and `"abc` throw `ERR_DSL_SYNTAX`.
  - **Precedence**
    - `NOT a==1 AND b==2` parses as `(NOT a==1) AND b==2`.
    - `NOT (a==1 OR b==2)` and `NOT NOT x==1` work.
  - **Null semantics**
    - `missing == null` is `true`.
    - `missing != "x"` is `true`.
    - `x.y.z == null` is `true` when `x` is missing.
    - `null > -1`, `undefined <= 5` and `NaN >= 0` are all `false`.
  - **BatchIngestor**
    - Concurrent `ingest` calls with a slow sink never overlap.
    - Delivery is in order, with no drops or duplicates.
    - A sink that rejects while new ingests arrive restores the batch ahead of the new items.
    - The watermark and `totalCommitted` are unchanged after the failure.
    - A retry delivers everything in seq order.
- Run `grep -rE "eval\(|new Function" src/` and confirm it finds nothing.

content.text:
I fixed both files, and `npm test` now passes all 11 tests, including the visible ones.

I also ran a quick scratch check of the new behaviour. `missing == null` and `missing != "x"` are true, and `null > -1` is false. `NOT a==1 AND b==2` parses as `(NOT a==1) AND b==2`. `"a\"b\n"` decodes correctly, and a dangling escape or an unterminated string throws `ERR_DSL_SYNTAX`. I did not test the concurrent-ingest path or `NaN` comparisons. The only check there is the visible test's reject-then-retry case. `grep` finds no `eval(` or `new Function` under `src/`.

**`src/queryDsl.mjs`**
- **Strings:** the tokenizer now decodes `\\`, `\"`, `\n` and `\t`, so `"C:\\temp\\"` ends cleanly as `C:\temp\`.
- **Unknown escapes:** any other escape, such as `\x`, also throws `ERR_DSL_SYNTAX`. You didn't specify this case; I chose to reject rather than pass the character through. Say so if you'd rather it be lenient.
- **Precedence:** the parser is now layered as OR, then AND, then NOT, then primary, with `()` re-entering at OR. `NOT NOT x` works.
- **Nulls:** `==` and `!=` treat `null` and `undefined` as equal. `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` return `false` if either side is `null`, `undefined` or `NaN`.

**`src/batchIngestor.mjs`**
- **Serialization:** `flush()` now chains onto an internal promise queue, so `sinkFn` never runs concurrently and batches stay in order. A failed flush doesn't block later ones.
- **Rollback:** if `sinkFn` rejects, the batch goes back to the front of the buffer, ahead of anything ingested meanwhile. The watermark and `totalCommitted` stay as they were, and the error is rethrown so a retry delivers everything in sequence order.

I didn't touch `src/frozenWire.mjs` or `src/errors.mjs`, and I haven't committed anything.
